findings.title: HTTP client must use make_client() not direct httpx.Client instantiation
findings.explanation: ADR-006 requires all outbound HTTP calls to use make_client() from app.clients.http, which provides standardized 3s connect/10s read timeouts, 2 retries with jittered backoff on connect errors and 502/503/504, request-id propagation, and metrics. This ADR was adopted after February 11, 2026 incident where requests.get() without timeout hung worker threads for 9 minutes.
findings.recommendation: Create a client module in app/clients/bank_transfers.py built on make_client('bank-transfers') and expose a debit_merchant() function. Import and use that function instead of direct httpx.Client instantiation.

findings.title: Missing @idempotent decorator on money-moving POST endpoint
findings.explanation: ADR-004 mandates @idempotent decorator on all money-moving POST endpoints to require Idempotency-Key header and replay cached responses for duplicates with 24h TTL. This endpoint creates refunds and debits processing fees, both money-moving operations, making it critical to prevent duplicate charges when clients retry timed-out requests (as happened with EUR 1,240 duplicate refund in January 2026).
findings.recommendation: Add @idempotent decorator above @router.post on line 22, following the pattern in existing create_refund endpoint on lines 14-19.

findings.title: Processing fee calculated on wrong amount
findings.explanation: The fee is calculated on charge.amount_cents (original charge amount) instead of the actual refunded amount. Line 16 comment and PR description both state fee is '1.5% of the refunded amount', and the refund created on line 33 is for charge.refundable_cents, which may be less than amount_cents if prior refunds exist.
findings.recommendation: Change line 35 to calculate fee on the actual refunded amount: fee_cents = _processing_fee(refund.amount_cents) or fee_cents = _processing_fee(charge.refundable_cents).
